title: "My Irritable Bowel" - research into the effectiveness of an online training for people affected by irritable bowel syndrome
summary: In this study, people with irritable bowel syndrome aged 18-70 have the opportunity to take part in the online training course “My Irritable Bowel”. During the training they can learn what irritable bowel syndrome is, how they themselves can influence their symptoms and thus potentially improve their quality of life. In addition to participating in the training, we are also conducting an accompanying survey as part of this study. In this way, we want to investigate the effectiveness of the online training “My Irritable Bowel”, i.e. we want to investigate whether participation in the online training has an influence on variables related to  physical health (reduction in IBS symptom severity) and mental health (improvement in quality of life).

interventions.name: Intervention group: Participation in the online training “My Irritable Bowel” (dealing with irritable bowel syndrome symptoms with cognitive-behavioral therapy content and nutrition-related content; 9 sessions of ca 25 minutes plus individual practice time, 8-week period)
Active control group: participation in the “My Relaxation” online training program (progressive muscle relaxation; 9 sessions of ca 25 minutes plus individual practice time, 8-week period)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
+ Irritable bowel syndrome (at least mild symptom severity)
+ Access to a device with internet access (computer, mobile phone or tablet)
+ Sufficient knowledge of the German language
+ Consent to participate/consent and data protection declaration
Exclusion criteria:
× Participation in the previous pilot study on “My Irritable Bowel” (Dec. 2019 to May 2020)
× Current psychotherapy treatment
× Current suicidal tendencies in the last two weeks
× Substance dependence in the last 6 months (alcohol and/or drugs)
× Current pregnancy or breastfeeding
× Current or previous psychotic illness 
× Atypical warning symptoms that are likely indicative of an illness other than irritable bowel syndrome (blood in the stool, onset of illness over the age of 50, unexplained severe weight loss, unexplained recurring fever)
